messages:
maria: Heads up — hitting multiple quotas in us-west-2 that's blocking our GPU fleet expansion. Need increases for: provisioned EBS IOPS (account total), EBS snapshot create rate, and GPU instance quota (p4d + g5 family). Launch is scheduled Mon 09:00 PT, ETA for fleet to be live is EOD Mon.

sahil: copying cloudops. can you paste the numbers you need and why? will open support case once we have justification.

maria: numbers: p4d quota to 25 (currently 5), g5 to 80 (currently 20). EBS provisioned IOPS (io1/io2) account total -> request to 350000 iops. Snapshot create rate -> bump to 800/min. Reason: each p4d node will attach 3 io2 volumes @ 40k IOPS target during eval runs (heavy checkpointing), plus snapshot-based backups during CI. We measured throttling on the staging run this morning.

vivian: +1 urgent. cluster scheduler already queued ~40 jobs; if we can't scale we risk jobs queuing overnight. also observed increased snapshot failures in us-west-2 at 07:15 which matches when we hit the limiter.

cloudops: opened AWS support case. case id: 12345678901. asked for region: us-west-2, requested quotas: p4d -> 25, g5 -> 80, EBS provisioned IOPS -> 350000, snapshot rate -> 800/min, ENI soft limit -> 2500. payload sent with cost justification and architecture doc link: https://internal.redwood/reports/gpu-fleet-q2.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support: Case 12345678901 received. Request review SLA 48 hours. Please provide justification for sustained high IOPS and plan to limit burst.

maria: added justification in the case: sustained io from checkpointing and parallel model evals, we need deterministic performance for latency-sensitive benchmarks. attached cost/ROI and fallback plan (staggering snapshot windows, gp3 fallback plan).

cloudops: AWS asked for temporary mitigations while they review. Suggestions: 1) reduce per-volume IOPS to 30k where acceptable, 2) schedule snapshot window off-peak and stagger by AZ, 3) start instances in small batches (5-7) to avoid sudden quota hits. I'll coordinate rollout sequencing in the runbook.

sahil: for the ENI/instance limit we can also request to use ENA enhanced networking and verify IMDS settings, but AWS still needs the quota bump. also flagging cost: p4d on-demand ~30K/mo each — confirm finance OK.

vivian: quick mitigation timeline: we can delay heavy checkpointing to after warmup and use local NVMe caching for first 6 hours to reduce snapshot pressure. I'll add a flag in the job runner to disable large checkpoints during initial scale-up.

cloudops: AWS responded: provisional approval for p4d -> 20 and g5 -> 60 within 12 hours, EBS provisioned IOPS increased to 200000 pending full review, snapshot rate increased to 400/min. Full requested increases require review and may take up to 7 days. See update in case 12345678901.

maria: thanks — we'll revise the rollout: reduce target fleet from 25 to 20 p4d, lower per-volume IOPS to 30k temporarily, and stagger snapshot jobs. updating deployment playbook now.

vivian: can we get a temporary monitoring alert on snapshot throttles + EBS write latency? want early warning during ramp.

cloudops: added alerts to Console: /alerts/ebs-write-latency and snapshot-error-rate. alert thresholds: p50 write-latency > 25ms or snapshot-error-rate > 2/min. will notify #eng-oncall and the rollout channel.

maria: deploy delayed by 24h to Monday 09:00 PT -> Tuesday 09:00 PT. will notify customers on the internal schedule doc. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sahil: closing loop — I'll follow up with finance re: committed spend and open a follow-up ticket to request the rest of the quota if we need it after validation.

aws-support-bot: Case 12345678901: update logged. next status update expected within 24-48 hours.

maria: noted, will post results of the staging ramp here once we've validated.
